concepts.def: Plants make glucose from carbon dioxide and water using light energy, releasing oxygen.
Green pigment in chloroplasts that absorbs light energy.
Light, carbon dioxide and temperature can limit the rate of photosynthesis.
Pores in leaves for gas exchange, controlled by guard cells.
Needed for healthy growth, e.g. nitrate for proteins, magnesium for chlorophyll.
Used in respiration, stored as starch, or made into cellulose.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Plant Nutrition — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Plant Nutrition brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Plant Nutrition.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which structure stores water in plant cells?
options: Nucleus
Permanent vacuole
Mitochondrion
Cell wall
respiration
photosynthesis
protein synthesis
mitosis

mcqs.q: When you are too hot, what happens to the arterioles in your skin?
options: They vasodilate — more blood flows close to the skin surface, releasing heat to the environment by radiation.
DNA ligase reads the gene and translates it into protein.
The blood vessels move up to the surface of the skin to release heat.
Capillaries split open to release blood and cool the body.

mcqs.q: What is the role of DNA ligase when inserting a gene into a plasmid?
options: Capillaries split open to release blood and cool the body.
DNA ligase cuts the plasmid open so the gene can be inserted.
It forms phosphodiester bonds that join the gene to the cut plasmid, sealing the recombinant DNA.
DNA ligase reads the gene and translates it into protein.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Plasmodesmata”?
options: Plant cells have cell wall, chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole, unlike animal cells.
Channels between plant cells through which substances can move.
Large central sac of cell sap; helps keep cell turgid.
Contain chlorophyll; absorb light for photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Chloroplasts”?
options: Plant cells have cell wall, chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole, unlike animal cells.
Channels between plant cells through which substances can move.
Contain chlorophyll; absorb light for photosynthesis.
Outward pressure from water in the vacuole pushing against the cell wall — keeps plant rigid.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Turgor pressure”?
options: Rigid layer of cellulose surrounding the membrane; gives shape and support.
Large central sac of cell sap; helps keep cell turgid.
Outward pressure from water in the vacuole pushing against the cell wall — keeps plant rigid.
Channels between plant cells through which substances can move.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Distinctive features”?
options: Channels between plant cells through which substances can move.
Rigid layer of cellulose surrounding the membrane; gives shape and support.
Plant cells have cell wall, chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole, unlike animal cells.
Outward pressure from water in the vacuole pushing against the cell wall — keeps plant rigid.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Permanent vacuole”?
options: Channels between plant cells through which substances can move.
Rigid layer of cellulose surrounding the membrane; gives shape and support.
Outward pressure from water in the vacuole pushing against the cell wall — keeps plant rigid.
Large central sac of cell sap; helps keep cell turgid.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cell wall”?
options: Contain chlorophyll; absorb light for photosynthesis.
Plant cells have cell wall, chloroplasts and a permanent vacuole, unlike animal cells.
Rigid layer of cellulose surrounding the membrane; gives shape and support.
Outward pressure from water in the vacuole pushing against the cell wall — keeps plant rigid.

mcqs.q: A plant cell wall is ~0.1 µm thick. How many cell wall thicknesses fit across a 1 µm gap?
A destarched plant is left in light with one leaf inside a flask of soda lime (which absorbs CO₂). That leaf tests negative for starch. Which conclusion is supported?
options: Carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis.
Light is needed for photosynthesis.
Chlorophyll is needed for photosynthesis.
Oxygen is needed for photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: A variegated leaf (green and white areas) is tested for starch with iodine. Only the green parts turn blue-black. What does this show?
options: Chlorophyll is needed for photosynthesis.
Carbon dioxide is needed for photosynthesis.
Water is needed for photosynthesis.
Starch is made everywhere in the leaf equally.

mcqs.q: A plant is given a balanced mineral supply except nitrate. Which symptom is most likely?
options: Poor growth and yellow older leaves (lack of protein)
Purple leaves only
Faster growth than normal
No effect, as plants do not need nitrate

mcqs.q: Why must a leaf be boiled in ethanol before adding iodine in the starch test?
options: To remove chlorophyll so the colour change can be seen
To add starch to the leaf
To kill bacteria on the leaf
To make the leaf photosynthesise faster

sequence.def: Chlorophyll in thylakoids captures light energy
Water split into O2, H+ and electrons
Excited electrons pass along thylakoid carriers
ATP made; NADP reduced to NADPH
ATP and NADPH fix CO2 into glucose in the stroma
